intent: Compare private-school participation rates across income percentiles to determine how participation varies from the lowest to the highest income groups.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How does private-school participation vary from the lowest to the highest income percentile?

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: Private-school participation rate generally increases from the lowest income percentile (10th) to the highest income percentile (90th), rising from about 0.0199 to 0.0600.
units.computation: Compare the participation rate at the lowest income percentile (x=10, value=0.0199) with the highest income percentile (x=90, value=0.0600); the rate is higher at the highest percentile, with a general upward trend across the sequence.
accept: Participation is higher at the 90th income percentile than at the 10th percentile.
The line shows an overall upward trend from the lowest to the highest income percentile.
The rate rises from approximately 0.02 at the 10th percentile to approximately 0.06 at the 90th percentile.
reject: Participation is flat or decreasing from the lowest to the highest income percentile.
The highest participation occurs at the 10th percentile.
The chart shows no difference between low and high income percentiles.

optional_valid: The increase is not strictly monotonic; there are small fluctuations at lower percentiles.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for why participation increases with income.
Using the final row with empty x (point_order 48, value 0.6199) as an income percentile endpoint.
review_notes: The table includes a final row with empty x and value 0.6199; it is excluded from the trend basis because it is not an income percentile anchor.
The intent asks for variation from lowest to highest income groups, so one combined trend unit is sufficient.
